issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a land acquisition does not succeed solely because the decision rejecting objections was communicated after the acquisition declaration, if the objections were decided before the declaration.
material_facts: The competent authority heard the objectors and rejected their objections by order before the declaration of acquisition was issued.
The rejection order was communicated to some objectors only after the declaration was issued.
issues.conclusion: The later communication of the rejection order did not invalidate the acquisition because the objections had already been decided before the declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3C(2) and 3D(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956, the competent authority must hear and decide objections and submit its report before the Central Government declares the acquisition. The provisions do not make communication of the decision to objectors before the declaration a condition of validity.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: A person challenged an acquisition of land for a public project.
predicates.objections_decided_before_declaration: The competent authority heard and decided the objections before the government issued the acquisition declaration.
predicates.rejection_communicated_after_declaration: The competent authority communicated its decision rejecting objections to an objector only after the acquisition declaration was issued.

issues.definition: When an acquisition is challenged, a decision on objections made before the declaration is not invalidated merely because it is communicated afterward.

issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition notification is sufficiently descriptive when it identifies the land and makes further land plans and details available, and a later objection to its description may be rejected when no such deficiency was raised within the objection period.
material_facts: The notification identified the villages, survey and sub-survey numbers, nature, type, and area of the land proposed for acquisition.
The notification stated that land plans and other details were available for inspection at the competent authority's office.

The initial objectors did not claim that the description prevented them from effectively objecting; some landowners raised that claim only in later representations, outside the statutory objection period.
issues.conclusion: The notification was not vague, and the later complaint about its description did not require consideration because it was raised outside the prescribed period.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3A(2) and 3A(3) of the National Highways Act, 1956 require a brief description of the land and publication of the substance of the notification in two local newspapers. Section 3C(1) provides a 21-day period for objections. The notification supplied adequate particulars, and the later complaint was not made within that period.

rule.if: land_acquisition_notification_challenge and notification_identifies_land_particulars and further_land_details_available and no_timely_description_objection and later_description_objection_out_of_time

predicates.land_acquisition_notification_challenge: A person challenged a notification proposing the acquisition of land.
predicates.notification_identifies_land_particulars: The notification identifies the affected land by relevant location and parcel details and states its nature and area.
predicates.further_land_details_available: The notification states that plans or additional details of the affected land are available for inspection.
predicates.no_timely_description_objection: The objectors did not claim within the objection period that the description prevented them from effectively objecting.
predicates.later_description_objection_out_of_time: An objector first complained about inadequate description after the period for making objections had expired.

issues.definition: A land acquisition notification that identifies the affected land and provides access to further details is treated as sufficiently descriptive when no timely objection to its description is made, and a later objection may be rejected as out of time.

issues.legal_issue: A competent authority's rejection of land acquisition objections is not invalid merely because its order is not formatted like a judicial order, where it has heard the objectors, considered the substance of their objections, and given a reason for rejecting them.
material_facts: The competent authority gave objectors an opportunity for personal hearing.
The authority considered objections concerning affected buildings, hardship, alternative land, and the need for the proposed widening.
The authority rejected the objections on the ground that the land was necessary for widening the highway and the project could not proceed without it.
The order was not drafted in the form of a judicial order.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the objections could not be faulted merely because the order was not drafted like a judicial order by a legally trained person.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3C(2) of the National Highways Act, 1956 requires the competent authority to provide an opportunity of hearing and to allow or disallow objections by order. The Court held that the authority had addressed the substance of the objections and that the order's non-judicial form did not, by itself, invalidate the decision.

rule.if: statutory_land_acquisition_objection_challenge and objectors_given_hearing and authority_considered_objection_substance and authority_stated_project_need and order_not_judicially_formatted

predicates.statutory_land_acquisition_objection_cha: An objector challenged the competent authority's decision on objections to a statutory land acquisition.
predicates.objectors_given_hearing: The competent authority gave the objectors an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.authority_considered_objection_substance: The competent authority considered the substance of the objections made by the objectors.
predicates.authority_stated_project_need: The competent authority explained that the land was needed for the public project and that the project required the acquisition.
predicates.order_not_judicially_formatted: The competent authority's order was not drafted in the form ordinarily used for a judicial order.

issues.definition: When objectors are heard, their objections are considered, and the authority gives a reason based on the project's need, the rejection is not invalid merely because the order is not judicially formatted.

issues.legal_issue: Judicial review of a technically planned public infrastructure acquisition is limited, and unsupported allegations that an alignment was manipulated to favour others do not justify setting the acquisition aside.
material_facts: The landowners alleged that the highway alignment had been changed to protect properties connected to influential people and proposed using other available land instead.
They did not identify the persons allegedly favoured with sufficient particulars or provide material supporting the allegation of bad faith.

The highway authority was a professionally managed body with expertise in highway development and maintenance, and the project was planned after technical study considering traffic and public interest.
issues.conclusion: The allegations of bad faith and objections to the technical alignment were not established; the acquisition could not be set aside on those grounds.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Girias Investment Private Ltd. v. State of Karnataka (2008) 7 SCC 53, which referred to S.R. Venkataraman v. Union of India (1979) 2 SCC 491, State of Punjab v. Gurdial Singh (1980) 2 SCC 471, and Collector (D.M.) v. Raja Ram Jaiswal (1985) 3 SCC 1, and on E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1974) 4 SCC 3. Allegations of mala fides require particularized pleading and convincing proof; courts should not draw doubtful inferences from incomplete facts. The Court also held that courts are not equipped to decide the feasibility of a specialist infrastructure project's alignment and that review is limited, permitting intervention where the project is ex facie contrary to law or tainted by proved mala fides.

predicates.public_infrastructure_land_acquisition_c: A person challenged a land acquisition undertaken for a public infrastructure project.
predicates.specialist_authority_planned_project_aft: A specialist public authority planned the project after technical study of relevant factors, including public needs.
predicates.alignment_mala_fides_alleged: The challenger alleged that the project alignment was manipulated to favour others or cause the challenger loss.
predicates.allegation_lacks_particulars_and_support: The challenger did not identify the alleged beneficiaries with sufficient particulars or provide material supporting the allegation.

issues.definition: A challenge to a specialist-planned infrastructure acquisition does not succeed on an alignment-based allegation of bad faith when the allegation lacks particulars and supporting material.
